title: Let documents.mjs revision --check name a check the change's coverage adds
description:
Found 2026-09-27 recording readable-views-2's receipts: `node .shady2k/documents.mjs revision --check views-check` fails with 'the policy has no check views-check' although a change's Coverage may name checks the policy does not list (views-check, readability), whose receipts stand on the whole revision. The refusal hint of runCheck already prints the whole revision for them. Worked around by recording those receipts against `documents.mjs revision`.

## Done when
revision --check <id> prints the whole revision for an id the policy does not pin (or refuses only an id no policy entry and no coverage could name, saying so), a test covers it, and the integration's receipt instructions say which command to use.

title: Read the whole product in its wiki, from vision to code, with backlinks and open questions
description:
Outcome 3 of knowledge-base (charter docs/milestones/knowledge-base.md, decision 0016); adopted from the deferred 'Show views per environment and architecture state', whose deployment views per environment are part of it. The wiki gains a product section (vision, roadmap, status, requirements, decisions, glossary) linked to the architecture with backlinks; where each requirement, use case and decision came from, with its quote, and on each source page what grew from it; a page per use case with its sequence diagram and its status computed from evidence (planned, partly built, built); a data catalogue (per entity: where it is created, stored and consumed, which flows and topics carry it, which zones it crosses); deployments per environment (stands, environment variable names, external integrations); and an open-questions section listing what is missing, who can answer, what stays incomplete and where the answer goes, with completeness per role.

## Left out
Views per architecture state; a portal over several repositories; editing in the wiki.

## DONE WHEN
madarch's wiki builds; every requirement page shows its scenarios and elements, every element page its use cases, requirements and decisions; a use-case page shows its sequence diagram and status; a requirement citing a fixture transcript shows the quote and links to the place in it, whose page lists the requirement; the reference system's data catalogue shows each entity's creators, stores, consumers, topics and zones; the open questions list the corpus's gaps, an explicit 'not applicable' closes one and an empty answer does not; the built site has no broken links.

title: Isolate every test run in its own scratch home and temporary folder, so no suite leaves anything in the owner's home or the system temporary folder
description:
Found 2026-09-30 during the wiki run: about 87 000 folders named madarch-* had piled up in the system temporary folder (63 490 of them madarch-model-check-*), left by test suites outside the wiki (test/model-check-repo.ts fixtures and others); together with other projects' caches the disk reached 99-100% twice in one night. The wiki's own suites were fixed in madarch-7br.3.2; the rest were not in that task's scope.

Widened 2026-10-09 (owner): during madarch-rtr.2.3 a test ran `madarch new` without a scratch home and left 377 draft folders in the owner's real ~/madarch/products. Cleanliness that depends on each test remembering to redirect its paths fails again; the run as a whole must be isolated.

## Approach (owner's choice, 2026-10-09)
A test preload declared in bunfig.toml (`[test] preload`) creates one fresh scratch folder per `bun test` run and points HOME, MADARCH_HOME and TMPDIR (and any other home-derived path madarch reads, such as MADARCH_WIKI_CACHE) into it before any test file loads, and removes it when the run ends. Spawned commands inherit it. A container was considered and set aside: tests spawn git, bun and Chromium, which a container would have to carry, and CI would differ from local runs.

## Done when
after bun test (full suite, performance tests included) nothing new exists in the owner's home (~/madarch included) or in the system temporary folder, apart from the wiki's content-keyed caches if they are kept on purpose (a check before and after); a test that writes to a home or temporary path without redirecting it lands in the run's scratch folder; the scratch folder is gone after the run, pass or fail; a committed test proves the preload is active (HOME and MADARCH_HOME point inside the scratch folder).

title: Make the reference system's views readable
description:
Decided by the owner on 2026-09-25 after looking at the merged views of madarch-mk5. Rendered by GitHub's own Mermaid renderer in a 1150 px column (a wide screen), 5 of the 8 pages show arrow labels under 12 px (the landscape 7.8 px, storefront 8.3 px, fulfilment 9.6 px, platform 11.7 px, ordering 11.9 px) and 7 of 8 have labels overlapping each other or a box. Causes: merged labels of up to 103 characters widen the diagrams; a topic's consumer is drawn as an arrow into the broker, named for what it does, so it reads as sending; the broker gathers every arrow; in an element's own view the general relation is drawn from the frame instead of its refinement from the module that does it; merged labels mix publishing and consuming in id order.

## Done when
On every page of the reference system rendered by GitHub's Mermaid in a 1150 px column, arrow labels
are at least 12 px and no label overlaps another label or a box (measured by rendering every page
and recorded with the numbers); every arrow carries its row number and every relation behind it is
in that row of the table under its diagram; a topic's publishers and subscribers are marked
(action: send | receive), their arrows drawn from the initiator, dashed, and entered by role; in an
element's own view its module's refinement is drawn, not the general relation from its frame;
likec4 validate and the Mermaid parse still pass.
(Rewritten 2026-09-27 by the owner's decisions: arrows from the initiator instead of from the broker
(madarch-48x.1), and numbered arrows instead of word labels after measurement.)

## Left out
Direct producer-to-consumer arrows through a topic (a derived relation, a later decision); views per environment or state; the server.
close_reason: Criterion met on 6c8f709 (the rewritten Done when): all 8 pages 13.1 px or more with no overlaps, numbered arrows with every relation in the table, publishers and subscribers marked and dashed, the module's refinement drawn, likec4 validate and the Mermaid parse pass. Stage madarch-48x.2 accepted; PR #2 merged by the owner.

title: Decide how the model marks a topic's or queue's consumer
description:
A decision the owner holds (asked 2026-09-25). In the format, publishing to and consuming from a topic are written alike (a relation from the service to the broker naming the topic interface); only the relation's name tells them apart, so a renderer cannot draw an event from the broker to its consumer.

Options: (1) an optional relation field consumes: true for a consumer of a topic or queue interface (a small, explicit format addition; relations without it unchanged); (2) no format change: event relations drawn dashed and labelled with the topic, arrow direction unchanged; (3) inferring from the name: fragile, not recommended.

Recommendation: (1).

Affects: the task that draws events from the broker to the consumer. Meanwhile the labels and the refinement tasks proceed.
close_reason: Owner decided 2026-09-27: an optional relation field action: send | receive on relations through a topic:: or queue:: interface (Codex's proposal, after AsyncAPI 3). Arrows stay drawn from the initiator (from -> to, as every other arrow), labelled by role: 'publishes <topic>' or 'subscribes to <topic>', dashed; no reversed arrows (owner, citing C4: the initiator's arrow).

title: Let a worker claim a task whose same-stage prerequisite is implemented but not closed
description:
Found in the graph-foundation run (2026-09-24). The protocol treats an implemented prerequisite inside the same stage as satisfied, but br refuses both 'br update --claim' and '--status in_progress' on an issue with an open blocking prerequisite. The coordinator had to set only the assignee, so every stage task after the first showed as open while a worker was on it, and the claim was not atomic.

## Done when
the integration's claim operation (and the adapter's ready) lets the coordinator hold a same-stage dependant of an implemented, integrated prerequisite as active under the worker's name, atomically, without removing the recorded dependency; proved on a scratch copy of the tracker. Normally a dependant of an open, unimplemented prerequisite still cannot be claimed.

## Left out
Changing br itself; cross-stage prerequisites (still need acceptance and closure).
close_reason: Done by the setup 0.26.0 update (madarch-kwe): node .shady2k/adapter.mjs claim holds a same-stage dependant of an implemented, merged prerequisite atomically through br, keeping the edge, and refuses otherwise; proved on a scratch tracker in .shady2k/adapter.test.mjs.

title: The wiki's Starlight engine fails to build when the wiki cache root is the default under the owner's home folder
description:
Found 2026-10-02 standing both engines' wikis of the reference system up for example.

What a person does: builds a wiki with the Starlight engine and no MADARCH_WIKI_CACHE set, so the cache root is the default under the home folder (XDG ~/.cache/madarch/wiki).

What happens: the build exits 1 with the engine's output: astro/vite refuses with "No cached compile metadata found" for @astrojs/starlight/dist/components/Page.astro, and the main-module id it names is mangled — the project root joined onto the cache's absolute path with its leading slash dropped (source/home/dev/.cache/madarch/wiki/template-…/node_modules/…). The same happens under node 24 directly, so it is not the bun runtime.

What should happen: exit 0 with the built site's path (capability wiki, requirement result).

Measured on this machine (same template, same pages, only the named variable changed):
- project under /tmp, node_modules symlinked at the default cache under /home/dev/.cache: build fails;
- project under /tmp, node_modules symlinked at a cache under /tmp (MADARCH_WIKI_CACHE, as the tests move it): build passes, 90 pages;
- the same project, node_modules copied (not symlinked) from the failing /home/dev/.cache install: build passes, 82 pages.

So the trigger is the engine's symlinked node_modules (linkStarlightNodeModules in src/wiki/starlight.ts) resolving into the default cache location, likely a path mishandling in the pinned astro 7.3.5 / rolldown-vite. Untested: whether a project folder also under the home folder fails the same way.

Workaround while deferred: point MADARCH_WIKI_CACHE at a folder outside the home cache (the gated tests already do).

title: Keep the query engine's buffer pool from filling under thousands of updates without a rebuild
description:
Found 2026-09-30 by the rework worker of madarch-ti6.2 (change server-views), measured with LadybugDB 0.20.4 under Bun 1.4.2, every query result closed.

## What was measured
- The engine's update path (update -> removeRelation/closeEdge, inserts) grows RSS about 115 KB per update call; with no reads in the loop and a rebuild every 500 calls, the 256 MiB buffer pool is exhausted ('Buffer manager exception: Unable to allocate memory! The buffer pool is full and no memory could be freed') after 5 032 updates and 10 rebuilds. At 2 000 calls RSS climbs linearly from 126 to 356 MB.
- Closing results does not change it (169 157 against 172 506 bytes per call, within noise); reads amplify it through statement churn but do not cause it.
- The read path is bounded: 24 000 dependents and view calls plateau near 160 MB.
- The engine opens new Database(':memory:', 256 MiB, false, false, 4 GiB), so autoCheckpoint stays at its default; the mechanism (WAL, version pages, allocator retention) is not yet known.

## Why it matters, and why not now
The MVP's server updates a graph's engine once per model sent and rebuilds it at start, so thousands of updates between restarts are far off; a server receiving models from CI or webhooks (live-graph) would reach it within days.

## Done when
The cause is found (a checkpoint, a periodic rebuild from the history, or a LadybugDB defect reported with a reproduction), and a test of at least 10 000 updates with rebuilds, yielding between batches, stays under a stated memory bound, skipped with the performance tests.

comments.author: claude-coordinator:shady2k@vm-agents:feature/registry-integrity

Deferred out of live-graph's outcome 1 by the owner, 2026-10-07 ("Я предлагаю этим заняться позже, это нас не блокирует" / "Убери это требование"). Revisit before outcome 3 (madarch-tah) starts: a server fed by CI reaches the bound within days.

Where it stood (run madarch-l19, worker l19-3-mem, 2026-10-02): growth is linear on the update path, ~10.3 MB per 250 updates (137 -> 294 MB over 4000, heading past the 400 MB bound); a disk-backed engine did not help; a smaller buffer pool makes LadybugDB fail. A probe rebuilding the engine from the history every 1000 updates plateaus at 185-192 MB with identical answers: the retained memory is the engine's, not the data's. Proposed mechanism, not yet decided: rebuild the engine from the history when growth exceeds a budget (e.g. +64 MB over its build). Open: the cause inside LadybugDB (not reported upstream); rebuild cost and its peak on a large model (measured only on a one-element model). The measured test and the probe are uncommitted in the worktree ~/.herdr/worktrees/madarch/w-l19-3-memory (test/query-engine-update-memory.test.ts, probe-rebuild-cycle.ts).

title: Let the wiki's agent improve itself through the product's own skills, each change replayed on past cases and accepted by the owner
description:
Idea from the owner, 2026-10-09: the wiki's agent improves itself. Each product repository already holds `skills/`, the team's own skills for that product, which is the natural first place.

Three levels, rising in risk: (1) the product's own skills: the agent sees it is corrected the same way again and again and proposes a change to a skill in `skills/`; (2) the shared skill set, another repository, reached the way a skills issue is filed today; (3) madarch's own code, as a feature run. At every level the change goes through the same path: a tracked task, a pull request, a replay on recorded past cases showing it does better and breaks nothing, and the owner's acceptance. Without that measure it is drift, not evolution.

Related: the owner's lifemodel project changes its own code by commits with an automatic revert; see the idea on lifemodel as the first outside agent.

Would show it is worth it: corrections of one kind stop recurring after the agent's own change to a product skill, measured on the replay.
Left out: changes to another repository without its own review and acceptance.

Where they meet: the agent-access milestone (MCP and API, madarch-yhy) could take lifemodel as its first outside agent and be accepted on its real work with the wiki, not a synthetic client. Its proactivity fits the wiki: noticing open questions, stale documents and unanswered comments.

title: Make the query-engine long-run memory check independent of what ran before it in the same process
description:
Debt found 2026-10-09 during the madarch-rtr run (stage 1 acceptance), on this machine, while running
the project's full stage checks. It is pre-existing and off that feature's path; nothing in that
change touches the query engine or its tests.

## What was measured
`test/query-engine-long-run.test.ts` asserts the whole run stays under 400 MB
(`expect(Math.max(...curve)).toBeLessThan(400)`). That number is measured on the **process** that runs
it, so it depends on what ran before it in the same `bun test` process:

- the file alone: RSS 159-163 MB, curve flat (slope -0.14 MB/batch), passes;
- the same revision, `bun test test/query-engine-performance.test.ts test/query-engine-long-run.test.ts`
  in one process, perf file first: RSS 436-440 MB, curve flat (slope 0.05, thirds gap 0 MB), **fails**;
- the whole suite (`bun test`, 1234 tests across 55 files): RSS 608-620 MB, curve flat, **fails**.

In every case the shape is the bounded one the test exists to prove (a flat plateau, a small
prepared-statement cache); only the absolute level differs. CI on GitHub runners is green for the same
full suite.

## Why it matters
A required check that is red on the development machine while the file alone is green makes every
stage acceptance ambiguous: the reader cannot tell a real regression from the process's accumulated
allocations, which is exactly the case this test should decide.

## Done when
The check decides the same thing wherever it runs: its bound is measured against a baseline the check
itself establishes (RSS at the start of its own curve, or a bound per batch), or the long-run file is
run in its own process by the check that requires it, and the full suite is green on this machine.

comments.text:
Decision (gap closed alone), coordinator, 2026-10-08: the change makes a current requirement false unless the model history carries the new compiled arrays, so madarch-hnq.1.4 is added to stage 1 to close it.

What I found: src/history/assertions.ts decomposes a compiled model into one assertion per kind of seven (element, interface, relation, category, zone, environment, state) and assembles a model back from exactly those kinds. compiled-model/shape gains entities and scenarios (madarch-hnq.1.1, .1.2), so a compiled model holding them would be stored without them and would not read back as compiled — which is exactly what the current requirement model-history/lossless promises. The change's Coverage does not name model-history, and its Preserved contracts do not either, so this was an oversight in the change, not a decision against it.

Why I did not stop: the alternative closures both need the owner. Filing the limitation as debt and leaving model-history/lossless false would be a weaker acceptance, and correcting that spec sentence would be a new delta in the change record, which changes its approval digest and would need a fresh approval. Carrying the new arrays through the history keeps every present document true and leaves the change's decisions untouched.

What I decided: entities and scenarios are each source's exclusive claim, like elements, interfaces and relations (CLASHABLE_KINDS), not shared vocabulary like zones, categories, environments and states. A second source declaring an existing entity or scenario id is refused, naming the id and the other source; a data entity is a repository's own declaration of its data, and a use case is one repository's, so silently merging two declarations would be worse than refusing.

Where it lands: task madarch-hnq.1.4 under stage 1, after madarch-hnq.1.2, in src/history/** and src/adapters/**, with the change record's Tasks line extended (the Tasks line is not part of the approval digest, so the owner's approval of 2026-10-08 still stands; the feature document check is clean).

title: Read the product's pages in the wiki in a comfortable typography and layout: navigation, focus mode and design tokens the editor will share
description:
Added to idea-to-wiki by the owner on 2026-10-09, in conversation, as a scope addition (recorded in the charter's scope decisions). The owner likes the typography of Zettlr, a Markdown editor for the desktop, and wants the wiki to read like it.

Starts after madarch-rtr lands: the wiki app (wiki/app, React 19 + Vite + react-markdown) exists only on that feature's branch, and today it has no stylesheet at all, so every page shows the browser's default HTML.

The work:
- a short research first (to-research): the typography Zettlr ships (fonts, measure, line height, heading scale, vertical rhythm, quotes, code, lists, tables) and the screen-typography guidance it rests on, from primary sources;
- shared design tokens: font families, a type scale, spacing, colours, a light and a dark theme following the system setting; kept in one place so the editor of madarch-j0a reuses them;
- the layout shell (added by the owner the same day, see the comment): a left navigation of the product's documents grouped by kind with the current page highlighted, the document in the centre, a focus mode hiding the panels, the navigation in a menu on a phone, and a closed place for the right context panel;
- the reading styles of the home page and of a document page built on those tokens: a text column of about 60 to 75 characters, line height about 1.5, a heading scale with a steady rhythm, readable quotes, code blocks, lists and tables.

Zettlr is GPL-3.0: its ideas are taken, not its code, stylesheets or fonts under a licence madarch cannot carry.

## Done when
In the browser walk of a fixture product holding headings of every level, paragraphs, a list, a quote, a code block, a table and a long line, each page's text column measures 60 to 75 characters, body line height is 1.4 to 1.6, no element overflows the column at 1150 px and at 390 px width, the dark theme follows the system setting, every page of the fixture is reached from the left navigation in one click with the current one marked (visually and by its accessibility attributes), the focus mode hides both panels and brings them back, and on a phone the navigation opens from a menu without narrowing the text; the numbers are recorded with the walk. A page rendered with the browser's default styles, or a value outside those ranges, disproves it.

## Left out
Search (madarch-o0d); the context panel's content (madarch-fe1, madarch-0uc); the editor, the Markdown and history modes and any editing (madarch-j0a, next milestone); the chat (madarch-cuu); the diagram tabs' own styling; the static Starlight export; a theme switch inside the app.

title: Record madarch's diagnosability conventions: log levels, request and trace ids, error causes
description:
Found in the setup 0.40.0 run (madarch-f9w), by the setup skill's diagnosability item: the repository records no conventions for what a log line carries at each level, how a request or trace id is threaded through the server, or how an error keeps its cause; and nothing says which of them a test or a review may rely on. The server is being built now, so the convention is cheapest to fix before more code follows it.

## Done when
the conventions are recorded where a contributor finds them (a decision record or the architecture document): the log levels and what each carries, how a request and a trace id are made and threaded, how an error preserves its cause and reaches a caller, and what a failure shows on CI's first screen; the server's existing code and tests follow them.

title: Make madarch's checks and messages independent of the unrelated nocx repository
description:
Found 2026-10-07 while resuming madarch-l19: the run's coordinator spent most of an hour trying to rebuild a checkout of nocx to run the server e2e test. The owner: "Почему это тест требует репозиторий nocx? Наш репозиторий не имеет к nocx никакого отношения."

## What is wrong
madarch's checks and texts depend on nocx, an unrelated repository of the owner:
- test/server-views-e2e.test.ts (added f93b9bc, 2026-10-01, as the server-views acceptance) sends nocx's model from a local nocx checkout named by MADARCH_NOCX and pinned to commit 3f0e46e (source github.com/shady2k/nocx). The model it sends lives on branch madarch-skill-run in the nocx repository. Without that checkout on this machine those tests cannot run; on another machine they never can.
- Product error messages give "github.com/shady2k/nocx" as their example: src/server/http.ts (~302, 459, 588), src/server/sources.ts (~134-140), src/send/send-model.ts (doc comment ~126).
- Current specs and records name it: docs/system/capabilities/server.md scenarios, docs/glossary.md:108, docs/decisions/0013; tests test/send-model.test.ts, test/server-sources.test.ts, test/server-http.test.ts.
Origin: the MVP charter revision c59db20 (2026-09-24) chose nocx as the real repository for the skill's one-time check (madarch-utk); the server-views run then turned that one-time acceptance into a permanent test.

## Done when
- The server e2e test builds its second source itself: a fixture git repository it creates in a scratch folder, with a model that passes the check, sent with the real send command. No outside checkout and no variable naming another repository; the test runs on any clone under MADARCH_SERVER_E2E=1.
- Product messages, current specs, the glossary and tests use a neutral example name (github.com/acme/shop, which the spec already uses); `grep -ri nocx src test scripts docs/system docs/glossary.md` finds nothing.
- Disproved by: any test that needs a path outside the repository, or a product message naming nocx.

## Left out
- History stays as it is: closed change records (docs/changes/*), the MVP charter and decision records describe what happened then.
- The branch madarch-skill-run in the nocx repository: deleting it is the owner's call in their repository; ask, do not do it as part of this work.

title: Link a product's work to an external tracker such as Jira: its items and status on the wiki's pages, then a two-way sync
description:
Owner, 2026-10-09 (decision 0017): many teams work in Jira and similar trackers. An external tracker is another adapter beside the product's own tracker. First step: a requirement, feature or stage keeps the external item's id and the wiki shows its status, madarch reading the tracker and never writing to it. Second step: a two-way sync for teams that work there, features and stages created there from the wiki and their status brought back, with one system of record for each item and each field, decided before the sync starts.

## DONE WHEN
a product requirement page shows the Jira issue linked to it with that issue's current status, read from Jira; a status changed in Jira shows on the page after the next read.

comments.text:
The set published setup in a product repository (skills-k8c part a) in shady2k-skills plugin 0.91.0, setup 0.41.0 (github.com/shady2k/skills main, 8a4c2e0).
- product.mjs adds `repo add <folder> <name> <url> [--branch <b>] [--json]` (enters a code repository in workspace.yaml's repos with one commit, every other byte kept; refuses a bad name, a duplicate, an unreadable manifest, a folder that is not its own git repository, uncommitted changes, a missing or option-like url; a failed commit restores the manifest) and `where [<folder>] [--json]` (product, code with the product root and repository name, or none; exit 2 on an unreadable manifest).

- The path from an empty folder: new, setup in the draft, rename, repo add, bootstrap, setup in the code repository. test/product-walk.test.mjs covers the programs end to end; setup itself is an agent-run skill with no code test.
This is what outcomes 2 and 5 of idea-to-wiki rely on for the commit check in a product repository and the first code repository. Moving write-intended-model (part b) is not scheduled.

title: Check a repository's product corpus with one versioned contract file
description:
Outcome 1 of knowledge-base (charter docs/milestones/knowledge-base.md, decision 0016). madarch's document contract (vision, requirements, decisions, glossary, the intended model with its scenarios and data entities, sources such as transcripts of conversations with product owners and the business, a path mapping for documents kept elsewhere) has its source in madarch and is built into one dependency-free file with --version, which a repository runs to check its corpus; the model check is part of it. The model skill lives in shady2k-skills and calls the installed file; madarch keeps no copy of it.

A requirement, a use case or a decision cites the source it came from by a quote and a place in it (a time or a line range); a source is kept in the repository or outside it, where the corpus keeps the quote and a reference.

## Left out
The skill set's own work (asking at setup where sources are kept and how they are redacted, its setup installing the file, onboarding, a documents-only mode) is tracked in its own repository.

## DONE WHEN
the built file, copied into a clean checkout of madarch, accepts madarch's corpus and prints its version; a broken corpus fixture is refused naming the file, the line and what is wrong; a fixture whose documents live at other paths passes through its mapping; a citation whose quote is not at the place it names in a source kept in the repository is refused naming both, and one to a source kept outside is reported as not verified; skills/write-intended-model is gone from madarch and madarch's model is checked by the contract file installed from the skill set.
close_reason: Moot by decision 0017 (owner, 2026-10-09): the per-repository contract file is dropped; the contract is madarch's checked write and commit path, now outcome 2 of idea-to-wiki (madarch-fe1)

The contract file installed in each repository holds no graph: it loads, compiles and checks, and gives model.json. The madarch engine is installed once per machine (a package or a container) with LadybugDB (a 29 MB native library per platform): the local graph in a cache outside git, the wiki, a local MCP. title: Store the graph on a sound foundation
description:
The formats and storage everything else stands on: the intended-model YAML format (nesting to any depth; environments with bindings, zone differences and which elements each has; a chain of architecture states; no rules or flows yet), its compilation into model.json, the storage of every model version with valid and recorded time from the first write in SQLite, and LadybugDB as the query engine built from it, answering the views' traversals (collapse to the visible level, drill-in, transitive dependencies) with the time filter. Includes the walking skeleton: Bun (pinned 1.4.2), TypeScript, TypeBox, strict YAML, static and test commands. Decisions 0002, 0005, 0006, 0009, 0014, 0015. No HTTP server.

## DONE WHEN
conformance tests pass for the review's scenarios (a service gains internal elements and its relations keep their meaning; a service moves to another domain and its id and references stay; one request carries different data categories each way; two environments have different endpoints and zones; a general relation and its refinement are not counted twice); a model using environments and states compiles and is stored without loss; as-of reads on both time axes through the query engine return the expected graph.
close_reason: Outcome criterion holds on main: conformance scenarios pass end to end from YAML to query answers, a model with environments and states is stored and read back without loss, as-of reads on both axes through the query engine return the expected graph (bun test 322 pass, CI green at b82c517); change graph-foundation passed acceptance and close document checks

# Product wiki direction: strong thesis, dangerous breadth

## Judgement

**Verdict:** pursue a narrow pilot, not a company platform yet. The defensible promise is an evidence trail from *why* a product change exists to the task, scenario, code change and later drift, with a useful human page at each point. A git-backed wiki with an agent is not by itself a differentiator; fewer stale answers and faster safe changes would be.

**What is strong.** Decision [0017](docs/decisions/0017-product-wiki-as-source-of-truth.md) puts intent and work in one product-owned repository, separate from restricted code, and gives local and central users the same git truth. This can give people portable knowledge, reviewable history and exits from the service. Decisions [0003](docs/decisions/0003-federation-by-normalized-contract-ids.md) and [0004](docs/decisions/0004-source-agnostic-core-with-fact-plugins.md) give federation a concrete join key and require sources plus coverage, rather than pretending an AI has understood every repository. This is more useful than another chat over documents *if* the chain is accurate.

There is genuine leverage already: [src/model/schema.ts](src/model/schema.ts) defines scenarios, entities, evidence and contract-bearing interfaces; [src/check/model-check.ts](src/check/model-check.ts) checks evidence, stale blobs and scenario-to-requirement ids; [src/adapters/ladybug-engine.ts](src/adapters/ladybug-engine.ts) and [docs/system/capabilities/graph-queries.md](docs/system/capabilities/graph-queries.md) support time-filtered dependency queries. [src/wiki/build.ts](src/wiki/build.ts) builds static Starlight/Zensical pages with link checks, and [src/server/http.ts](src/server/http.ts) stores sent models and serves view text. These are foundations, **not** a writable product wiki or a code index. The accepted [wiki capability](docs/system/capabilities/wiki.md) still says a repository's `README.md` and `docs/` become read-only pages; the [server capability](docs/system/capabilities/server.md) explicitly has no authentication and never reads a repository.

**What could fail.** The biggest change is custody. Today's [model check](src/check/model-check.ts) assumes the model, evidence blobs, code and capability requirements are in *one* git repository; [0017](docs/decisions/0017-product-wiki-as-source-of-truth.md) separates them. Cross-repository pins, permission-aware references, links across rewritten history and missing code access all need real semantics. Also, [docs/vision.md](docs/vision.md) still excludes a wiki editor and calls the old installed contract the direction: it is not evidence that the new editor exists. The first milestone should explicitly replace those contracts, not silently promise both.

Non-engineers may prefer a familiar, forgiving editor to Markdown, branches and merges. A chat does not fix weak navigation, formatting, mobile access, rich tables or notification habits. Git excels at a modest number of durable reviewed changes, not multiple people editing the same paragraph, live comments and a commit per small chat turn; automatic rebase can alter the intended meaning, while a rejected push makes a successful-looking edit disappear. A revert creates a *new* commit; it is neither a guaranteed one-click reversal of dependent edits nor erasure of secrets or harmful text from git history.

An agent that applies without confirmation makes every prompt-injected document, ambiguous instruction and broad rewrite a production write request. Limit its tools, context, path set and transaction size; show the diff **after** a successful bounded commit with obvious undo, and escalate destructive, permission-changing and cross-page edits before executing them. A pretty diff is not sufficient if the commit is attributed to a human without a verifiable actor: git `author` is metadata, not authentication. Give people per-product roles, a server credential and an audit record for human/agent identity; authorize every read, query and write, including source snippets and cross-product graph traversals. Git history and indexes retain personal or confidential material even after page deletion; test deletion and redaction procedures before ingesting transcripts.

The current [server](docs/system/capabilities/server.md) is localhost/no-auth and accepts uploaded compiled models; central multi-tenant reading, auth, isolation and git-backed writes are new systems. The current [history store](src/adapters/sqlite-history.ts) is authoritative for received model assertions and LadybugDB is derived from it, not rebuilt directly from the product repo; [0017](docs/decisions/0017-product-wiki-as-source-of-truth.md) changes the source of truth. Specify what happens to recorded-time history on replay, force-push, bad commits and index lag. The many moving parts—editable wiki, agent runtime, permissions, git collaboration, skills/tracker migration, own code index, federation and company abstractions—are several products, not one two-week milestone. A single owner with agents still pays integration, operations and support costs.

**Competition.** Notion AI already edits workspace pages and searches connected tools, while Confluence AI/Rovo drafts content and can create Jira work; “chat next to a page” is not a moat ([Notion AI](https://www.notion.com/help/notion-ai-faqs), [Confluence AI](https://www.atlassian.com/software/confluence/ai)). More pointedly, [GitHub wikis](https://docs.github.com/en/communities/documenting-your-project-with-wikis/about-wikis) and [GitLab wikis](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/wiki/) are already separate Git repositories with browser editing, and GitHub/GitLab have issues and PR/MR links. [Backstage TechDocs](https://backstage.io/docs/features/techdocs/) publishes Markdown from code-adjacent repositories; [Linear Agent](https://linear.app/docs/linear-agent) creates and updates work. These are not proven equivalents to a checked intent→scenario→code→history graph, but madarch must compete on **trusted evidence and cross-product impact**, not storage format, basic editing or AI chat. Integrate with existing work systems before trying to replace their best workflows; actual substitution remains a pilot hypothesis.

### Assumptions worth trying to kill cheaply

| Assumption | Cheapest test and failure signal |
| --- | --- |
| A non-engineer will maintain the product source in this wiki | Give a PM and analyst each one real edit in a clickable page prototype, unassisted; observe completion time, errors and whether they return the next week. |
| A requirement-to-code link written at task launch is useful and stays honest | Trace one recent feature from requirement through a real task and PR; have a second engineer find the code without guidance. Flag links that have no reviewed code evidence. |
| One git repo handles team edit traffic | Simulate 10 editors on two different pages and the same page against a bare test remote; count retries, lost edits, elapsed save time, and legible conflict resolutions. |
| Instant agent commits are welcomed and reversible | Put a one-page, non-sensitive bounded agent edit in front of three users; log wrong changes, undo success, correction time and trust afterwards. No default access to broader pages. |
| Agents can use organisation models within budget | Meter tokens and spend for 20 real edit/comment requests; ask the budget owner for a per-team cap and a no-model fallback. |
| Per-product access can be enforced across wiki, snippets and graph | Threat-test a user with product A access but not product B against page search, graph traversal and agent context; any B content returned fails. |
| Contract ids can connect the team's actual repositories | Label ten real provider/consumer interfaces from two repos, compare normalized ids and explain unmatched ones; do not treat missing extraction coverage as absence ([0003](docs/decisions/0003-federation-by-normalized-contract-ids.md), [0004](docs/decisions/0004-source-agnostic-core-with-fact-plugins.md)). |
| A separate product repo can preserve evidence to code after movement | Move one real scenario/evidence chain from the old in-repo model to a pinned code ref; test rename, changed file, inaccessible repo and force-push. |
| The wiki can replace or coexist with the team's task tool | Run one real task in both places for a week; compare duplicate-entry time, missed updates and whether the team chooses the wiki next time. |

## Creative ideas

1. **[Quick win] A “why is this here?” button on each page and code-linked element.** Show the smallest chain from source quote or decision through requirement, scenario and task to a reviewed change, with the commit and evidence status. A newcomer gets an answer they can check instead of a generated paragraph.
2. **[Quick win] A change receipt rather than an AI summary.** Every agent edit gets an actor, base revision, paths, intent, validation result, diff and undo link on the page. A PM can inspect exactly what happened after an immediate change without understanding git.
3. **[Quick win] A landing page of unanswered decisions, not a generic dashboard.** Group broken citations, missing owners, unanswered comments and uncertain code links by the person who can resolve them. A team can spend ten minutes a week closing concrete knowledge gaps.
4. **[Quick win] “Is this still true?” on a requirement.** Show last edited time, last linked code change and index coverage side by side, explicitly “unknown” when code was not indexed. A product owner sees where to ask for review without mistaking freshness for correctness.
5. **[Quick win] Import as pointers, not migration.** Mirror a small read-only set of existing pages and tasks from the team's current tools, then invite editing only the three canonical pages needed for the pilot. People can try the new links without being forced to abandon familiar habits on day one.
6. **[Bet] Task launch as a trace envelope.** Starting work binds a task to requirement/scenario ids; the eventual PR and changed symbols enter a pending evidence list for human review. Engineers stop reconstructing “why” months later, while a task is never declared implemented merely because a file changed.
7. **[Bet] Drift as a question, not a red warning.** When code changes outside linked work, show candidate affected requirements with coverage and confidence, then ask the owner to link, amend or say unrelated. This can reveal undocumented change without turning every rename into a false alarm.
8. **[Bet] A contract boundary map with two-sided ownership.** For each normalized contract id, display provider, consumers, code refs, declared obligations and the last two teams to change it; preserve “unmatched” as a visible state. A cross-team change gets a contact and an impact path before release.
9. **[Bet] Rehearse a proposed change over a disposable graph.** Overlay a branch's code and a draft requirement, then list scenarios and dependent contracts that would change, with evidence and index gaps. Teams can discuss impact without publishing speculative assertions as truth.
10. **[Bet] Incident rewind with two clocks.** Compare what the team *believed then* against the code and deployments believed to be in use at the incident, and label the gaps. An on-call engineer can distinguish a stale model from a new regression; this depends on preserving valid and recorded time honestly.
11. **[Bet] A bounded assistant for structured edits.** Give the page chat a typed job such as “add an alternative flow to this scenario,” scoped to that page and known ids; reject references that do not resolve. Users get conversational editing without giving an agent arbitrary repository write rights.
12. **[Moonshot] Company-wide “who breaks if we retire this?”** Traverse product manifests and federated contract ids into ownership and business-use-case impact, with visibility filtered for the asking person. A platform team sees a defensible retirement plan rather than an organisation-wide hairball.
13. **[Moonshot] Reusable intent patterns across products.** A company-level abstraction could describe a common flow or policy once and show which product scenarios conform, diverge or have unknown coverage. It helps governance only after several products have proven the same vocabulary; do not start by inventing an ontology.

## The two-week first slice

Choose **one willing product team with one PM/analyst and one engineer**, one existing product, one code repository and one real change underway. Success at day 10: the PM can change a requirement without using git; the engineer can open its page and reach the scenario, task, accepted PR/commit and a pinned code file/line; both can see who changed it and undo a bounded bad edit. A newcomer can answer “why does this feature exist and where is it?” in five minutes, and at least two participants choose to use the wiki again unaided. Measure edit latency, conflict rate and agent cost, not just page views.

- **Days 1–2:** make a small separate product repository with a manifest pinning that code repo and three canonical pages: one requirement, one scenario, one active task. Reuse current model/schema and link checks where they fit; bridge the old in-repo evidence rather than claiming it is already portable. Keep the team's current task tool as an external link.
- **Days 3–7:** add one authenticated product-scoped write path for a Markdown page and a narrow page-chat instruction, both using the same validation and git commit transaction. Compare the client's base commit or blob before saving; different pages serialize cleanly, a same-page conflict is shown as a conflict, **never silently overwritten**. Commit with server identity plus verified human actor metadata, display the diff and provide revert with conflict checks. Rebuild the affected page promptly and the whole site asynchronously, showing last indexed commit.
- **Days 8–10:** run the real change through the wiki, have three people edit or review, exercise simultaneous edit and malicious page instruction, then inspect links and failures together. Stop or simplify if users cannot finish an edit, incorrect agent commits are hard to spot/undo, or evidence cannot survive the repo split. Keep a human-written fallback for a stalled agent.

**Leave out:** multi-product federation and company abstractions; automatic whole-code indexing, deep call/data flow and computed implementation status; full tracker/skill-set replacement; realtime co-editing; transcript ingestion; rich editing; unrestricted agent tools; public deployment/SSO and enterprise permission matrices. Do not expose this pilot to sensitive documents or other products. This slice tests [0017](docs/decisions/0017-product-wiki-as-source-of-truth.md)'s risky user/write path while using the accepted graph instead of rebuilding every layer at once.

## Questions before chartering, in order

1. **Who is the first real team, and what exact weekly job will they move?** If nobody volunteers a PM/analyst and a live change, start with a facilitated prototype, not infrastructure.
2. **Is the wiki replacing work tracking or linking to an existing tracker first?** Replacement requires lifecycle, notifications, permissions, reporting and skill-adapter migration; linking keeps the pilot small.
3. **What may the server agent commit without prior approval, and on whose authority?** Define path scope, action limits, destructive cases, audit identity, undo window and spending ceiling before a write API.
4. **Which documents and graph edges may each role read, including cross-product answers and source snippets?** Strict separation changes indexing and federation design; if all pilot content is public internally, say so explicitly but do not infer enterprise safety.
5. **What is a durable link to code when the wiki and code are different repositories?** Decide pinned refs, symbol/file anchors, force-push behavior and who confirms inferred links; this determines the graph schema and drift claims.
6. **Must two people edit the same page at the same time?** If yes, git per commit plus optimistic rejection may not meet the UX bar; test co-editing or reconsider the store. If no, conflict detection and a clear retry path are enough to start.
7. **Where do model calls run, who pays, and what happens offline or when the provider fails?** This changes the promise of “same locally and centrally” and whether a no-model editor is mandatory.
8. **What is the measurable reason to use this instead of the team's existing tools?** If traceability does not save real time or prevent a real mistake in the pilot, narrow the product to evidence/impact rather than building a general wiki.

**Source note:** The requested `README.md` is absent in this checkout; I used the named decisions, vision, glossary, capability specs and `src/` instead. The pre-existing working tree modification to `.beads/issues.jsonl` was not touched.

## 1. Recommendation

1. **No candidate fits: build the wiki thin inside madarch.** No engine meets requirements 1, 3 and 4 together — the git-native wikis (Gollum, OtterWiki, the Gitea/Forgejo wiki, SilverBullet) have no pre-write validation gate and no comments, and every rich wiki (Wiki.js, Outline, Docmost, BookStack, XWiki) makes a database authoritative instead of git.
2. **Keep madarch as the store and the write path**: the web UI calls madarch's own HTTP/MCP handler, which runs the document contract check first, refuses an invalid document, and only then writes the file and commits it with `git commit --author=<person>` in the product repository.
3. **Take the editing surface off the shelf, not the wiki**: CodeMirror 6 (MIT, plain-string document) for the first feature — the bytes that go in come out — with a madarch-rendered preview beside it; a WYSIWYG mode (MDXEditor, MIT, MDAST↔Lexical, string in and out) can come later as a per-user choice that rewrites a page deliberately (no WYSIWYG keeps Markdown byte-faithful).
4. **Comments as files beside the page** (one YAML file per thread per page, committed by the same path); git-bug is the closest prior art for sync semantics, but it stores in refs, so madarch defines this small format itself.
5. **Keep Starlight/Zensical as the read-only export and mermaid 12 for diagrams**, add Pagefind/Orama for search and better-auth/Auth.js for sign-in; the computed pages stay madarch's own work on the graph, not a wiki feature — so the next milestone's first feature should be the **write path**: edit a page, check it, and refuse it or commit it as its author, with the comments format and the local/central split following.

## 2. Candidate × requirements

Notation: **M** meets, **P** partly (with the reason), **B** breaks (with the reason). Requirements, abbreviated: **1** git is the store; **2** web edit = commit by its author; **3** validated before write, invalid refused; **4** comments in git next to the page; **5** computed pages + Mermaid; **6** agents write by the same path (madarch MCP); **7** same engine local and central, sync by plain git; **8** leaves madarch's LadybugDB graph alone; **9** TypeScript on Bun.

Notes on the table:
- Requirement 8 is "the wiki engine must not replace madarch's graph": a candidate **breaks** it when it keeps its own content database or graph tables (Wiki.js, Outline, Docmost, BookStack, XWiki, TinaCMS) and **meets** it when it holds no store of its own (Gollum, the Forgejo wiki, the CMSs' git mode, Starlight/Zensical).
- Requirement 9 is a cost, not a veto: Ruby/Python/Go/PHP/Java engines add a second runtime and a second write path that madarch cannot validate.
- "Comments" for the CMS row means page discussion; Bitbucket PR comments and Gitea labels are workflow status, not discussion.
## 3. The parts, if the app is thin

Everything below was read from the project's own docs/source or its registry metadata on 2026-10-09. The write-path invariant that makes the parts safe: **parse the candidate document to validate it, then write the original bytes to disk and commit them** — never re-serialize a page from an editor's internal model on the write path, because the serializers normalize (mdast-util-to-markdown's defaults rewrite bullets to `*`, quote marks and list indentation: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/syntax-tree/mdast-util-to-markdown/main/readme.md).

### Editor (the page surface)
- **CodeMirror 6 with `@codemirror/lang-markdown` 6.5.2** (MIT, 2026-08-04; the `codemirror` meta package is 6.0.2): a plain-string document, so what goes in comes out; the only transformations are ones a plugin applies. Source: https://registry.npmjs.org/@codemirror/lang-markdown
- **`@codemirror/lint` 6.9.7** (MIT, 2026-06-09) to show the contract check's findings at their line and column in the editor. Source: https://registry.npmjs.org/@codemirror/lint
- Optional later, per-user WYSIWYG: **MDXEditor 4.3.2** (MIT, 2026-10-02) — it converts MDAST ↔ Lexical, states "there is no intermediate HTML representation of the markdown document. The component accepts and emits markdown as a string", and ships a diff/source mode (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mdx-editor/editor/main/docs/overview.md, `.../docs/diff-source.md`). Alternative: **Milkdown 7.22.2** (MIT, 2026-09-23), whose source of truth is the ProseMirror document and whose output is remark-formatted (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Milkdown/website/main/docs/guide/faq.md). **TipTap 3.31.4** normalizes on serialize and its comments/review extensions are paid (https://registry.npmjs.org/@tiptap/markdown, https://tiptap.dev/pricing/). **BlockNote 0.55.0** documents its Markdown export as lossy and its `xl-*` packages as GPL-3.0/commercial (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TypeCellOS/BlockNote/main/docs/content/docs/features/export/markdown.mdx).
- Consequence for the recommendation: the byte-faithful surface is a source editor; WYSIWYG is a deliberate re-format of the page, which madarch can allow as a mode, not as the only way to write.

### Markdown parser and validator (the pre-write gate)
- **remark / unified**: `remark-parse` and `remark-stringify` 11.0.0 (MIT, 2023-09-18) over the documented **mdast** tree, with the plugin ecosystem for frontmatter, GFM and directives (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/remarkjs/remark/main/readme.md, https://registry.npmjs.org/remark-parse).
- **`remark-lint`** (MIT) — about 70 rules with presets, emitting `line:column` messages (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/remarkjs/remark-lint/main/readme.md); a project-specific rule is one remark plugin over the same AST.
- **`vfile-message` 4.0.3** (MIT) is the message type the check returns: `place` with `line`/`column`, plus `fatal`, `ruleId`, `source` (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vfile/vfile-message/main/readme.md) — exactly the "file, line and what is wrong" the contract check already promises.
- YAML side: **Ajv 8.20.0** (MIT) gives `instancePath` (a JSON Pointer) and `params` per error (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ajv-validator/ajv/main/docs/api.md); madarch already validates with typebox 1.3.34 (`package.json`), and a line number for YAML needs the parser's own position map (madarch has `src/model/yaml-position.ts`).
- Optional canonical form, if madarch wants byte-stable pages: **Prettier's `--check`** fails when a file is not formatted (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/prettier/prettier/main/docs/cli.md), with `proseWrap` defaulting to `preserve` so prose lines are not rewrapped (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/prettier/prettier/main/docs/options.md).

### Mermaid
- **mermaid 12.1.0** (MIT, 2026-10-02; madarch pins 12.0.0) draws in the browser. Server-side SVG needs a browser: **`@mermaid-js/mermaid-cli` 12.0.0** (MIT, 2026-09-24) launches Puppeteer (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mermaid-js/mermaid-cli/master/src/index.js). Measured here on Bun 1.4.2 with mermaid 12.0.0: `mermaid.parse` succeeds in-process, `mermaid.render` fails with "document is not defined"; madarch's own AGENTS.md already records headless Chromium with puppeteer-core working on this machine. Sources: https://api.github.com/repos/mermaid-js/mermaid/releases, https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid-cli

### Search
- **Pagefind 1.5.2** (MIT, 2026-04-12): it indexes the built static output and has no server component (https://pagefind.app/docs/) — the right part for the Starlight/Zensical export madarch already builds.
- **MiniSearch 7.2.0** (MIT, 2025-09-16): in-memory full-text, "can comfortably run both in Node and in the browser" (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lucaong/minisearch/master/README.md) — rebuild from git at boot; the least moving parts for a local wiki.
- **Orama `@orama/orama` 3.1.18** (Apache-2.0, 2025-12-19): in-process full-text/vector/hybrid for a long-lived server index (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oramasearch/orama/main/README.md).
- All three keep their index as derived data, so none becomes more authoritative than git.

### Auth (who the edit is attributed to)
- **better-auth 1.7.7** (MIT, 2026-09-30), framework-agnostic TypeScript auth (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/better-auth/better-auth/main/README.md); alternative **`@auth/core` 0.41.3** (ISC) used as a library, since `next-auth` v5 is still beta (5.0.0-beta.32, 2026-07-20).
- The honest limit, from git's own docs: author and committer names "have no effect on authentication" (https://git-scm.com/docs/git-commit), and GitHub's vigilant mode marks a commit "Partially verified" exactly when author ≠ committer (https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/managing-commit-signature-verification/about-commit-signature-verification). So madarch can attribute an edit (`git commit --author="Name <mail>"`, committer = the server, plus a trailer naming the person) and can sign with the **server's** key to prove the server wrote the commit; proving that the *person* authored it needs that person's key and is out of scope for a wiki whose trust model is the repository's own access control.

### Git access, concurrent edits, merge
- **The real `git` binary through `simple-git` 4.0.2** (MIT, 2026-09-26), with **one writer queue per repository** because git serialises index updates with lock files (`core.lockfilePid`, https://git-scm.com/docs/git-config). This is what keeps requirement 7 true: SSH remotes, credential helpers and hooks behave exactly as when a person runs git (https://git-scm.com/docs/gitcredentials, https://git-scm.com/docs/githooks); `--author`, `--date`, `--no-verify` and `-S` are documented options of `git commit`.
- **isomorphic-git 1.43.2** (MIT, 2026-10-08) is the fallback when no CLI is present (browser-only workspace, tests): `git.commit` takes author and committer objects and can sign via an `onSign` callback, but it speaks HTTP(S) only (SSH URLs are rewritten), runs no `.git/hooks`, ignores submodules and has no partial clone or wire protocol v2 (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isomorphic-git/isomorphic-git/main/src/utils/translateSSHtoHTTP.js, `.../docs/onPrePush.md`, `.../src/commands/checkout.js`, `.../docs/faq.md`).
- Concurrent edits: **`git merge-file --object-id -p`** merges three blobs with no worktree or index, and **`git merge-tree --write-tree`** merges commits without touching the working tree (https://git-scm.com/docs/git-merge-file, https://git-scm.com/docs/git-merge-tree). A pure-JS equivalent is **node-diff3 3.2.1** (MIT, 2026-06-03); the older `diff3` package is dead (0.0.4, 2022-07-25, https://registry.npmjs.org/diff3). **Yjs** (13.6.33) and **Automerge** (3.5.0), both MIT, are only worth using as the editor's live layer: neither ships a Markdown/git adapter and their merge authority is the CRDT document, not the files (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yjs/yjs/master/README.md, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/automerge/automerge/main/README.md).

### Comments (there is no part to take)
- No candidate stores per-page discussion in git. The closest prior art for the *sync* half is **git-bug** (GPL-3.0, v0.11.0 2026-09-22), which keeps issues and comments in git refs so they travel with `git push`/`pull` (https://github.com/git-bug/git-bug); **git-appraise** stores reviews as git-notes and is unmaintained since 2023 (https://github.com/google/git-appraise, https://git-scm.com/docs/git-notes). So the comments format — one YAML file per thread beside the page, committed by the same path — is madarch's own small contract.

### The agent path (same write path)
- **`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.32.1** (MIT, 2026-10-05, https://registry.npmjs.org/@modelcontextprotocol/sdk): the MCP server and the web UI call the same handler, so requirement 6 costs a transport, not a second write path.

### What stays unchanged
- **Zensical 0.0.69** and **Starlight 0.42.6** remain the read-only export: today's `src/wiki` already produces engine-neutral pages and hands them to either engine; a thin app adds a live surface beside them and does not replace them.
## 5. Citations

title: `madarch new` creates a draft product repository with its constitution, its manifest and its git history
description:
Outcome 1 of idea-to-wiki (charter docs/milestones/idea-to-wiki.md). Change `draft-product` (docs/changes/draft-product/change.md), capability product-repository.

A draft product repository is what a person with only an idea starts from: a real git repository holding the product's constitution, its manifest with a stable id, and the folders the wiki, the model, the skills and the prototypes live in. This stage delivers its creation and reading; the wiki that opens on it is stage 2.

## Done when
In a scratch products home, `madarch new` leaves `products/idea-YYYY-MM-DD` a git repository with one commit holding `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `workspace.yaml`, `.gitignore`, `docs/`, `model/`, `skills/` and `prototypes/` and an untracked `repos/`; it prints the folder and the product's id; a second run that day creates `idea-YYYY-MM-DD-2` with its own id; a products home or an argument that cannot be used exits 2 naming it and creates nothing.
close_reason: Stage 1 accepted 559b0c7, extended to 7c69fb8 by its supplementary note; stage 2 accepted 559b0c7 to f74e9c6. All tasks of both stages closed on their acceptance records; the finding madarch-rtr.2.5 stays open by the closer decision: a planning lesson for future runs, not this feature behaviour.

title: Repair the four madarch new tests that read the day in the test process zone, not the command s
description:
Found 2026-10-10 while closing madarch-rtr out: four tests in test/product-cli.test.ts fail on this machine between 21:00 and 24:00 UTC (00:00-03:00 MSK), and pass the rest of the day.

bun test runs the test file's own process in UTC whatever the machine's zone is (probed on bun 1.4.2: new Date().toString() inside bun test is GMT+0000 with TZ unset, and GMT+0300 for the same script outside it). The file's todayName() therefore reads the UTC day, while the child it spawns (bun scripts/madarch.ts new) inherits no TZ and reads the machine's local day, which is what the product's own rule uses (change draft-product, "The draft's name": idea-YYYY-MM-DD, of the day's date, from the local date). The two disagree whenever the local date differs from UTC's, so the assertion folder === idea-<todayName()> fails.

Evidence, this machine (TZ Europe/Moscow), 2026-10-09T21:27Z, on the landed revision 4be4f96:
MADARCH_SKIP_PERF=1 bun run test -> 1264 pass, 34 skip, 4 fail of 1302 tests across 58 files. All four are madarch new tests:
- test/product-cli.test.ts:172 expected /tmp/madarch-cli-elsewhere-m0HF4P/idea-2026-10-09, received /tmp/madarch-cli-elsewhere-m0HF4P/idea-2026-10-10
- test/product-cli.test.ts:184 (--home=FOLDER), :335 (--home with spaces) and the --home over MADARCH_HOME case, the same way.
CI is green on the same revision because GitHub's runners are UTC, where the two clocks agree.

## DONE WHEN
MADARCH_SKIP_PERF=1 bun run test is green on this machine at any hour: the command's child process is given the same zone the test file's own process reads, the test still asserts the rule (the day's local date), and the product's behaviour is unchanged.
close_reason: Accepted by stage madarch-rtr.1 (accepted: 559b0c7, extended to 7c69fb8 by its supplementary note); implemented records and receipts on each task.

title: Serve a product's wiki: its pages read from the working tree and the API the app reads
description:
Change `draft-product`, capability `product-wiki` (docs/changes/draft-product/capabilities/product-wiki.md), requirements `pages`, `live` and `result`; capability `server`, requirement `serves-wiki`.

Both halves of the read path, in one task:
- pages from the working tree: every Markdown file under the product's `docs/` and `README.md` at its root, ordered by code point of the path; a page's title is its first level-one heading, else its file's name without its extension; a page's text is read from disk on every call and never cached; the wiki's revision is a digest of the pages' paths and contents (so the same tree gives the same revision, and an unchanged wiki is never shown as changed); a path the wiki does not hold, and a path that climbs out of the product, are refused naming it;
- the server's product mode: `startServer` takes a product folder and/or a data folder, at least one, and offers each part's routes; `GET /api/product`, `GET /api/pages`, `GET /api/page?path=…`; the app's built files served from the app's folder; `index.html` for a path the app does not hold, so a page's address can be reloaded and linked; JSON refusals naming what was asked for; one log line per request carrying method, path, status and no document content. The server prints/returns the address it listens on, serves no wiki without a product folder, and refuses to start with neither.

Owned scope: `src/product-wiki/` (new), `src/server/wiki-app.ts` (new), `src/server/http.ts`, `src/index.ts`, and the test files for both halves. Tests go through the HTTP interface on a free port and through the page library, with fixture folders the tests create; the server's existing routes and their tests must keep passing.

## Done when
Tests show: the API lists the fixture's pages with their titles and the revision; a page's Markdown comes back whole; a missing page is refused with its path; a path under the app's routes answers `index.html`; the log line carries the method, path and status and no document text; asking twice after a file changes gives the new bytes; the product's files and git status are unchanged by every request. `bun run check` and the whole existing suite pass.

title: A task that spawns a long-running command and waits in its tests spends its session budget in those waits
description:
Found during the madarch-rtr run, 2026-10-09: task madarch-rtr.2.3 (the `madarch serve` wiring, one worker session) overran its 75-minute bound and was stopped with its work uncommitted and its own test file failing 6 of 18.

## What was measured
- The task bundled three mechanisms in one session: the wiki app built once on first use (its own toolchain and cache), the server started by a command that must keep running, and tests that spawn the real command and wait up to 20 seconds for it to serve.
- Its test file takes about two minutes per run, so the session's 75 minutes covered roughly twenty iterations, most of them waiting inside `whenServing` while the spawned command printed nothing and started no server.
- `bun run check` was clean and the sources were written when the bound tripped; only the spawned-command path never served.

## What it suggests
- A task whose tests spawn a long-running process and wait for a bounded timeout spends its budget in those waits: the task should either be split so the spawned-command path is its own task with a small test file, or name a much shorter wait and a smoke test beside the full one.
- A first-use build path (install and build a second toolchain inside the task's own checkout) is a task of its own when its failure mode is silent.

## Done when
The rule above is applied where it belongs (the task break-down or the brief), and a worker session that runs this shape of task finishes inside its bound, with a test that fails fast when the spawned command does not serve.

comments.text:
Decision 2026-10-10, by the closer at the feature's close-out: this finding stays open — it does not close with the run, and it is not this change's behaviour.

Why: its rule (a task whose tests spawn a long-running command waits in them; split the spawned-command path into its own task with a small test file and a short failing-fast wait, and never bundle a first-use build into it) applies to the planning of future runs, where there is nothing to apply it to today: the stage-2 tasks at 4be4f96 are done. It is genuinely new work on how tasks are briefed and sized, so it stays a finding in the milestone's queue, attached to this feature as its provenance. Whoever briefs the next run with a spawn-and-wait task or plans a first-use build should read it and its stage-2 measured numbers first.

The stage-2 test file since measures the spawned-command wait bounded (15 s in printedLiveFacts) — the failing-fast half of the rule exists; the task-shaping half still has no owner.

title: Close the stage-2 review findings on the page set
description:
Close the stage-2 review findings that touch the page set (src/product-wiki/pages.ts) — gpt-6.1-sol's round 1 over 559b0c7..HEAD.

- Blocker 2: the page set follows symlinks — `statSync` follows a root `README.md` symlink and `readdirSync` follows a `docs/` symlink, so `README.md → .beads/issues.jsonl` publishes tracker content and `docs → ../elsewhere` publishes Markdown outside the product. Validate the resolved target against the permitted places and refuse a boundary-crossing symlink naming both paths (the static wiki's documents reader already does this).
- Blocker 4: every directory-read error is swallowed as "no pages" and a README stat failure likewise, so an unreadable `docs/private/` silently shrinks the wiki and an unreadable `docs/` returns the successful empty digest. Distinguish absence from permission/IO/type failures and refuse with the full path and cause.
- Should-fix 11: the heading scanner recognises only backtick fences, accepts `#Title` as a heading, misses indented headings and keeps closing hashes; `scanDocument` in src/wiki/documents.ts already handles these rules — share it or match it.
- Should-fix 12: a link written as the wiki's own advertised address (`/p/docs/vision.md`) is treated as the held path `p/docs/vision.md` and shown as text; `a%20b.md` cannot reach `docs/a b.md`; and produced addresses are unencoded, so a `#` in a file name truncates the requested path.

Each finding is fixed with a test that fails on the previous revision, or argued down with the case that shows it is not real; `bun run check` and the product test files pass; the worker's report answers by number.

title: Close the stage-2 review findings on the server product mode and the command
description:
Close the stage-2 review findings that touch the server's product mode and the command — gpt-6.1-sol's round 1 over 559b0c7..HEAD.

- Blocker 3: the opener runs through unbounded `spawnSync` after the server starts, so an opener that stays alive (a foreground browser) blocks Bun's event loop for its lifetime and the printed address cannot answer; an opener waiting for that address deadlocks. Launch it asynchronously, handle launch failure without blocking serving, and manage its lifecycle.
- Should-fix 9: `startServer({ productFolder, port })` without an app folder starts an API-only server whose `/` answers 404, although the server requirement says a server given a product folder serves that product's wiki. Default to the checkout's built app or refuse to start with an actionable diagnostic.
- Should-fix 10: the SPA fallback answers any method on any non-API path, so a product-only server answers `POST /models` with 200 `index.html`. Restrict static serving to the methods it supports, restrict the fallback to the app's routes, and keep named 404/405 refusals elsewhere.
- Should-fix 13: command boundaries drop diagnostics — a manifest refusal loses the reader's file and line, and a builder launch failure reports `exit null` without the cause. Print the structured location and the launch error.
- Should-fix 14: the read-only test never initialises a git repository, so its `git status` check passes on a failed command with empty output, and the mixed-mode test sends no model and requests no view. Make both prove what they claim.
- Should-fix 15: `docs/system/architecture.md` still says the server never reads a repository and refuses to start without a data folder, and its new served-wiki paragraph omits the app folder and the command's first-use build. Make the document true of this revision.

## Done when
Each finding is fixed with a test that fails on the previous revision (documents proved by reading the code), or argued down with the case that shows it is not real; `bun run check`, the server and product test files pass; the worker's report answers by number.

title: Close the stage-2 review findings on the wiki app and CI
description:
Close the stage-2 review findings that touch the wiki app and CI — gpt-6.1-sol's round 1 over 559b0c7..HEAD.

- Blocker 1: the root `bun test` discovers the app's tests before CI has installed the app's dependencies, and the app imports `@vitejs/plugin-react` and `@happy-dom/global-registrator` without declaring either in its own package and lockfile (the installed root toolchain masks it). Declare what the app uses in `wiki/app/package.json`, update its lockfile, and make the CI order install the app's dependencies before any suite discovers its tests (or restrict the root suite to root tests).
- Should-fix 5: the proposal says a link to anything that is not a page of the wiki is shown as its text, and the app instead makes http/https/protocol-relative destinations clickable external links (a test enforces the contrary). Make the app follow the requirement.
- Should-fix 6: `setInterval` starts a new list request while earlier ones are pending and cleanup aborts none, so a stalled endpoint accumulates requests and an older response can overwrite a newer list and revision. Keep one poll in flight, abort on cleanup, and never let an obsolete response update state.
- Should-fix 7: a hidden tab stops polling indefinitely, so a page open in it goes stale past the two seconds the requirement promises for every open page. Poll regardless of visibility and refresh at once when visibility changes.
- Should-fix 8: a page fetch runs only on mount or path change, so one transient `/api/page` failure leaves the error on screen forever while the files stand still. Retry a failed page read independently of the revision, bounded.

## Done when
Each finding is fixed with a test that fails on the previous revision, or argued down with the case that shows it is not real; `bun --cwd wiki/app run check`, `bun --cwd wiki/app test`, `bun --cwd wiki/app run build`, the root `bun run check` and the whole suite pass; the worker's report answers by number.

title: Decide whether the server needs a restartable query-engine process
description:
A decision the owner holds, for the server of this outcome: whether the query engine must run in a separate process restarted after N queries or M megabytes.

## Corrected 2026-09-25
This decision was filed on a stage-3 reviewer's single measurement that read as a LadybugDB defect: memory growing by about 85 KB per recursive query with a time filter, flat without it. Checked since, that reading is wrong. The filter clause makes no difference; the growth comes from our own configuration, with LadybugDB's default of one execution thread per core and a new statement prepared for every query time, and from synchronous test loops that never let the runtime release dropped statements. The measurements and the fix are in madarch-ti6.2.

## Affects
The server of this outcome, which runs for days. Not views, the agent skill, or the foundation's correctness.

## Recommendation
No restartable process. Once madarch-ti6.2 lands, its long-run test shows whether memory levels off; if it does, the server holds one engine for its lifetime, rebuilt only when the history changes, and this decision closes on that evidence. If it still grows, the restartable process (rebuilt from the history, which is fast and exact) is the fallback.

## Meanwhile
Nothing waits on this before the server is built; madarch-ti6.2's result releases it.
close_reason: Owner decision 2026-10-01: not needed; the in-process engine is bounded (ti6.2 long-run evidence), the update path debt is madarch-8iw

title: Bound the query engine's memory by limiting LadybugDB's threads and not preparing a statement per query time
description:
Found 2026-09-25 while checking the recorded cause behind the server's memory decision (madarch-ti6.1). Measured with LadybugDB 0.20.4 under Bun 1.4.2 and Node 26, on a 14-core machine, 10 000 to 40 000 queries per run.

## What was measured
- The filter clause in a recursive query is not the cause: with and without it, memory grows the same and levels off (about 115 MB for 30 000 queries of a 200-node chain returning a count).
- Returning the path's relations (`rels(p)`, with or without `list_transform`) costs memory per execution thread. At the default thread count (one per core, 14 here) a process running `dependents` settles between 0.7 and 1.2 GB for a 50-element graph; with 1 or 2 threads (`new Connection(db, n)` or `setMaxNumThreadForExec`) it settles near 170 to 250 MB, and each query is about twice as fast (2.3 ms against 5.4 ms).
- `dependencyQuery` writes `valid`/`known` into the statement text (LadybugDB refuses `$parameters` inside a recursive relationship filter: "Cannot evaluate $_ because it does not depend on n or r", tried in five forms). A caller asking "now" through an advancing clock therefore prepares a new statement on every call: our engine at 2 threads, fixed time, stays at 253 MB over 40 000 calls; with an advancing time it climbs towards 1 GB.
- A prepared statement dropped by our code is released only when Node or Bun run its native finalizer, after garbage collection and an event-loop turn. A synchronous loop that never yields fills the 256 MB buffer pool within 10 000 distinct statements; with a yield every 500 calls 40 000 distinct statements plateau near 340 MB, under both runtimes. This is not a LadybugDB defect, and a server yields between requests.

## Done when
- the engine's connection runs with a small fixed number of threads (1 or 2, chosen by measurement);
- a query's `valid`/`known` are reduced to the latest time in the model history at or before them (the answer can change only at those times), so the statement texts are bounded by the history's size and the prepared-statement cache hits; the graph-queries conformance tests pass unchanged;
- a long-run test (at least 20 000 `dependents` and `view` calls with an advancing clock, yielding to the event loop between batches) shows memory levelling off under a stated bound, and is skipped with the other performance tests under `MADARCH_SKIP_PERF`;
- the code's statements that blamed LadybugDB are corrected: the engine's comments that a prepared statement is "never freed" and the B1 stability test's explanation of its growth (decision 0009 and `docs/system/index.md` were corrected when this was filed), and `docs/system/index.md`'s known unknown is updated to the measured result;
- an issue asking LadybugDB to accept parameters inside recursive relationship filters is drafted and shown to the owner; it is sent only with their yes.

## Left out
A worker process restarted after N queries (the open decision madarch-ti6.1 waits on this measurement); replacing the Node binding (the C API through Bun's FFI or the WASM build: both cost more and change nothing measured here).
close_reason: Stage acceptance recorded on the owning stage epic; merged to main at e7aff8b, specs replayed at 0c69682
